A1.justification: Both PDFs describe YOSO and contain readable text, equations, tables, and figures supporting comparison. v1 ends with references; v3 additionally contains Appendices A–G, which were included in the assessment.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 experiments and ablations, text-to-image fine-tuning results, and downstream application examples in Section 6.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds YOSO-LoRA-v2 results in Table 5 and a quick-adaptation experiment in Appendix F.

M1.justification: Section 5.1 adds decoupled adversarial and consistency schedules with different time gaps, k=250 and m=25, replacing their shared target timestep in v1's objective. Section 6.4 also introduces retraining on community-model/YOSO-generated data to produce YOSO-LoRA-v2. These change the training procedure beyond the retained latent discriminator, perceptual loss, IPI, and quick-adaptation components.

E1.justification: Figure 5 replaces the prompted turtle example with a null-prompt test of the text-to-image models, adding an evaluation condition without text guidance. CIFAR-10, JourneyDB, HPS, resolution transfer, image editing, ControlNet, and the named community-model coverage are otherwise retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes Score SDE (VP), Probability Flow (VP), and FastDDPM. Table 4 adds pretrained SD1.5, and Table 5 introduces an unaccelerated Realistic-vision reference comparison. The principal text-to-image comparators remain; newly discussed DMD is not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces an equal-budget comparison using 5,000 total iterations, including 1,000 adaptation iterations where applicable, with matched prompts and initial noise. Table 5 adds evaluations at different sampling budgets, while Table 4 drops one-step LCM-LoRA and evaluates SD1.5 at 25 steps. Existing benchmark metrics remain unchanged; newly disclosed training details do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix F and Figure 7 add a controlled ablation testing whether quick adaptation improves convergence under equal training budgets. Figure 5 adds a null-prompt case, and Section 6.4, Table 5, and Figure 6 investigate whether retraining improves one-step community-model compatibility. These substantially extend the retained CIFAR-10 and initialization analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, explicit random-seed values, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional results retain point-estimate and qualitative reporting; matching initial noise in Figure 7 supplies experimental control rather than uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes YOSO-PixArt-α's reported HPS/AeS from 28.21/6.18 to 29.83/6.14, placing its HPS above SDXL-Turbo's unchanged 28.91. Table 5 adds compatibility results, including one-step Realistic-vision with YOSO-LoRA-v2 at 27.13/6.12. Figures 5–7 also add or replace qualitative outcomes. These are revised or newly evaluated model results, not evidence of a controlled same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: v1's Equation 3 asserts an equivalence between marginal and joint KL objectives; v3's Equation 2 instead explicitly defines a joint KL formulation. Section 5.2 revises the teacher's v-prediction target to use its denoised estimate, and the final consistency objective revises the noise coupling and explicitly includes stop-gradient. These are local mathematical revisions; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: efficient one-step generation from scratch and pretrained models, one-step PixArt and LoRA capabilities, resolution adaptation, and downstream compatibility. Added methods and evidence do not materially redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: Section 6.4 adds a bootstrapping explanation for reducing distribution shift and improving compatibility, replacing v1's narrower remedy and discussion of full-fine-tuning style loss. It also attributes transfer failures partly to LoRA capacity. Appendix B newly states fairness, detail-generation, and object-count limitations, while the central self-cooperative mechanism interpretation remains.

D1.justification: Appendices C, D, and G add pseudocode, optimizers and betas, learning rates, EMA coefficients, clipping, loss weights, image selection, and synthetic-data filtering details. Section 6 adds training iteration counts and LoRA batch information. Reproducibility documentation expands substantially, although LoRA batch guidance is ambiguous between 64 in Section 6.3.2 and 256 in Appendix G.2, and v1's explicit no-augmentation statement disappears.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion of DMD and its relationship to variational score distillation, with new references to DMD, ProlificDreamer, and Diffusers. It removes the FastDDPM reference and v1's criticism of InstaFlow's fixed data-noise pairings. The general positioning against diffusion-GAN hybrids remains.

P1.justification: The main Sections 1–7 retain their sequence and much of their wording. v3 makes localized language and terminology edits, expands the introductory explanation, adds an author, and moves the general text-to-image related-work paragraph into Appendix E. The new appendix organization does not constitute a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially revised: Figure 1 corrects branch labels and gradient annotations, Figure 5 replaces comparison samples and its final scenario, and Figure 6 is rearranged and extended with LoRA-v2 outputs. v3 adds Table 5, Figure 7, and Algorithm 1, and revises existing table structures and headers. These changes extend beyond numerical updates or pagination.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens reproducibility and evidence for the text-to-image extension. Appendix G supplies previously missing training details, Appendix F tests quick adaptation under an equal total budget, and Section 6.4 provides evidence for addressing v1's acknowledged one-step transfer failure. Mathematical corrections also improve precision. LoRA batch-size ambiguity and absent uncertainty estimates remain, but the overall gain rests on better documentation and experimental support rather than higher reported scores alone.
